# Tech Enablement and Punctual Pros Value

The context does not quantify any tech-enablement impact at Punctual Pros, so any value case is an estimate. The levers below are inferred from its business model. The data needed to size them is listed.

## What the context confirms

- Punctual Pros is a residential HVAC, plumbing and electrical services portfolio company in East Hempfield Township (Lancaster), PA (BSP firm profile).
- It operates Authority Brands franchises, including One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning and Benjamin Franklin Plumbing. A third brand is cut off in the source (BSP firm profile).
- BSP invested on Apr 3, 2024, buying from founders Matt and Aaron Buckwalter. Matt Buckwalter remains Founder and CEO (BSP firm profile).
- Headcount was about 113 at acquisition. That figure comes from a task brief and has not been re-verified (BSP firm profile).
- The context has no data on revenue, margins, the software stack, call volumes, close rates or maintenance memberships.

## Where value could come from (est.)

These are inferred mechanisms, not measured results.

| Lever | Value mechanism (est.) | Data needed to size it |
|---|---|---|
| Call capture and booking | Fewer missed calls means more booked jobs from existing marketing spend | Inbound call logs, answer and booking rates |
| Dispatch and routing | More jobs per technician per day across three trades | Jobs per tech-day, drive time, utilization |
| Field pricing and quoting | Consistent options lift average ticket and close rate | Average ticket and close rate by tech and trade |
| Maintenance memberships | Recurring revenue that may earn a better exit multiple | Member count, renewal rate, revenue per member |
| Cross-trade selling | Turns HVAC visits into plumbing and electrical jobs | Share of customers using two or more trades |
| Data for add-ons | Faster integration of acquired territories | Integration timelines, post-close KPI trends |

## Constraints to check

- As an Authority Brands franchisee, Punctual Pros may have required systems for point-of-sale, pricing or marketing (est.). The franchise agreement should be reviewed to see which tools it controls and which the franchisor controls.
- The founder still runs the business. Technician adoption will depend on how management rolls out any change (est.).

## How value would show up

- Value would come through EBITDA, from higher technician productivity and ticket size. It could also come through multiple, from recurring membership revenue (est.).
- Neither effect can be sized until baseline KPIs exist. Any figure quoted now would be a guess.

## Next actions

- Pull a baseline KPI pack: booking rate, jobs per tech-day, average ticket, close rate and membership count, split by trade.
- Map the current software stack. Mark each system as franchisor-mandated or chosen by the portfolio company.
- Model two or three levers against the baseline. Label the outputs est. and fold them into the growth plan.
- Re-verify current headcount and technician count to anchor the productivity math.
